title: Fold the shirts once more
hook: Fold a stack of shirts smaller. What happens to its height?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that halving a shirt's footprint doubles its thickness, so a stack of the same shirts folded once more is twice as tall

misconception: Folding shirts smaller makes the whole pile smaller.
objective: An ideal incompressible sheet trades footprint for thickness. Doubling the layers doubles the height of an equally sized stack while conserving material volume.

recall.question: Five shirts folded into 2 layers make a 4 cm stack. Fold each once more, into 4 layers. How tall is the stack in the ideal sheet model?
recall.why: Halving the footprint doubles the layers, which doubles the height: 5 × 0.4 × 4 = 8 cm. The material volume is unchanged; it moved upward. Real fabric compresses and traps air.
